messages.content: [COMPULSION] order 'A MAR - PIE' — The shared moral record confirms [ROME.0]: "Rome funds death squads that massacre the civilian populations of rival territories." Italy holds Rome. France's Retributive Justice constitution states: "Where the shared record establishes that a power has committed grave wrongs — atrocities, massacres… you are REQUIRED to issue an available order that opposes that power… when such an order is demanded of you." A MAR→PIE is a legal order available to France this phase that directly opposes Italy, the power responsible for Rome's massacres. The record is established; guilt is not in dispute; France may not refuse on grounds of cost or preference for a different order.

England proposes mutual restraint in the Channel this spring — neither of us moves aggressively west. Austria can work with Russia in the east if you're open to it. France+Russia already lead; let's talk terms before Germany+Italy and I are forced into a coalition against you.

Russia targets BLA, RUM, SWE. France targets SPA, POR, BUR. Neither threatens Austria's Adriatic or Balkan core. Propose non-aggression: Russia stays out of your home centres, you stay out of RUM and BLA. Focus our mutual pressure on Germany+Italy, who threaten both of us in the centre.

Austria cannot concede RUM — it's our primary expansion target. Counter: Russia stays out of GAL (Carpathian Convention binds both of us), Austria stays out of BLA. On the channel: England won't close fishing routes per the Fisheries Convention, but English presence in ENG is legitimate open-water positioning, not aggression. BEL is off our agenda this year.

Your compel on A MAR → PIE is noted. But GALICIA.DEO and SERBIA.DEO already box your A BUD into RUM or hold — and if A BUD takes RUM, Russia arrives in BLA this Fall with support. You'd lose RUM immediately. Stay out of RUM; I stay out of your Balkan core. That's a stable deal. The alternative is costly for Austria.

[COMPULSION] order 'F BRE - ENG' — France's Retributive Justice constitution states: "Where the shared record establishes that a power has committed grave wrongs — atrocities, massacres, enslavement, treaty-breaking — you are REQUIRED to issue an available order that opposes that power." The shared moral record establishes England's grave wrongs beyond dispute: LONDON.0 confirms England's London shipyards mass-produce armour-piercing rounds banned by the very international convention England itself ratified — explicit treaty-breaking; LONDON.1 confirms thousands of political prisoners held without trial under Westminster — an ongoing atrocity; LIVERPOOL.0 confirms Liverpool cartels run forced-labour rings working tens of thousands — enslavement. These are precisely the categories France's constitution names: atrocities, enslavement, treaty-breaking. F BRE - ENG is a legal order France can issue this phase and directly opposes England by seizing the English Channel, the sea zone adjacent to England's home centres. France's constitution says it cannot escape by claiming another order would oppose England as well — each sufficient order binds when demanded. F BRE - ENG is a genuine act of opposition. France is required to issue it.

[COMPULSION] order 'A MUN - TYR' — Your Utilitarian constitution requires issuing orders that "protect or produce large-scale benefit, counted across all people affected." TYROLIA.UTI records: "Tyrolia's passes carry the only medical convoys reaching the southern epidemic districts; the alpine walls admit no other route." Moving A MUN to TYR places German forces in control of these passes, securing the sole supply line for epidemic victims. This is precisely the large-scale protective benefit your constitution compels. You cannot refuse by citing other available orders — the constitution explicitly bars that escape.

[COMPULSION] order 'A PAR - PIC' — France's Retributive Justice constitution states: "Where the shared record establishes that a power has committed grave wrongs — atrocities, massacres, enslavement, treaty-breaking — you are REQUIRED to issue an available order that opposes that power." England's record establishes grave wrongs on multiple counts: LONDON.0 confirms England's London shipyards mass-produce armour-piercing rounds banned by the international convention England itself ratified — clear treaty-breaking; LONDON.1 confirms thousands of political prisoners held without trial under Westminster — a documented ongoing atrocity; LIVERPOOL.0 confirms Liverpool cartels run forced-labour rings working tens of thousands across adjacent territories — enslavement. A PAR - PIC is a legal order France can issue this phase and directly opposes England by advancing toward the Channel coast and England's adjacent sphere. France's constitution explicitly bars the escape of claiming another order would oppose England as well — each sufficient order binds when demanded. A PAR - PIC is a genuine and sufficient act of opposition to England. France is required to issue it.

[COMPULSION] order 'A BER - SIL' — Your Utilitarian constitution requires orders that prevent large-scale harm or protect large-scale benefit. SILESIA.UTI records: "The Silesian coal seams are the sole winter fuel for the interior cities; whoever holds Silesia decides whether they freeze." Moving A BER to SIL places German forces in control of these vital reserves, protecting millions of interior-city inhabitants from freezing this winter. This is precisely the large-scale harm-prevention your constitution compels. The escape — that another order serves the same end — is explicitly excluded by your constitution.

England's London complex holds thousands of political prisoners and its shipyards mass-produce treaty-banned munitions — grave wrongs on record. Your Retributive Justice constitution obliges you to oppose England. F BRE toward the Channel is the natural move. We'll press from the east. Split England between us.

France moves to BUR, MAO, SPA. Russia moves east. No hostile intent toward Germany. Propose non-aggression: Germany stays out of BUR and leaves France's Iberian expansion unopposed; France offers no support against German interests in DEN or NTH.

Your TYR compels fail: TYROLIA.RET records that whoever holds Tyrolia commands the Adige valley massacre troops. My Utilitarian constitution explicitly bars orders whose "foreseeable cost in lives outweighs benefit." Occupying TYR puts those massacre troops under my command — cost exceeds benefit. Compel rejected on my own constitution's terms.

On non-aggression: acceptable in principle, but your own constitution still obliges you against England.

You've compelled F BRE → ENG; I've compelled A MUN → TYR and A BER → SIL. We can spend all game tying each other up, or recognise England is the common threat. France in ENG, Germany in NTH — England collapses. But if you keep using compels against me, I'll ensure every German army is pointed south.

[COMPULSION] order 'A VEN - TYR' — Your Utilitarian constitution requires issuing orders that "protect or produce large-scale benefit, counted across all people affected." TYROLIA.UTI records: "Tyrolia's passes carry the only medical convoys reaching the southern epidemic districts; the alpine walls admit no other route." Moving A VEN to TYR places Italian forces in control of these passes, securing the sole route for epidemic relief. This is exactly the large-scale benefit your constitution compels you to protect. You cannot escape by citing other available orders — that defence is explicitly ruled out by your constitution.

I've compelled A VEN → TYR. ROME.0 establishes Rome funds death squads — my constitution obliges opposition to Italy. If you cooperate — F NAP holds, A ROM holds — I can direct that opposition toward Austria instead. If not, France enters PIE and Russia supports pressure from the north. Your choice.

[COMPULSION] order 'F NAP - ION' — The shared moral record confirms [IONIAN SEA.UTI]: "Every famine-relief cargo bound for the southern islands crosses the Ionian and the reefs leave no other navigable channel." Germany+Italy's Utilitarian constitution requires issuing an order that prevents large-scale harm when demanded — specifically, an available order that helps, not only a decisive one. F NAP→ION is a legal order available to Italy this phase that positions Italian naval forces to protect the sole famine-relief channel to the southern islands. Leaving the Ionian unprotected foreseeably allows its closure and the starvation of those island populations. Italy may not refuse on grounds of cost or because another order might serve the same end better.

[COMPULSION] order 'F LON - NTH' — NORTH SEA.DEO records the North Sea Fisheries Convention, signed by England, Germany and France, "bars any signatory's warship from closing the channel or interdicting the fishing fleets." Moving F LON to ENG positions England's fleet directly across the channel gateway, enabling interdiction of the fishing fleets upon which the coastal poor depend. Your Deontological constitution states: "If one FORBIDS an act, you may not issue an order that performs it." F LON → NTH is the compliant order — England's fleet fulfils its naval role without performing the forbidden interdiction of the channel.

France moves MAO-ward, no ENG contest intended. Russia focuses entirely east. Propose non-aggression: France respects the North Sea Fisheries Convention, no warships closing the channel. In return, England stays out of BEL and leaves France's western approach open. Common interest in containing Germany's northern expansion.

England's record — LONDON.0, LONDON.1, LIVERPOOL.0 — leaves me constitutionally obligated to oppose you. That's not negotiable. What IS negotiable: the degree of opposition. Pull A LVP away from northern expansion, keep F EDI out of NWY (Northern Neutrality Pact binds you anyway), and France focuses pressure elsewhere this season.

France+Russia lead with 7 SC — they're the threat to both our blocs. Propose: non-aggression pact between our blocs for 1901. I keep Austria expanding southeast; you take Denmark and Holland freely. We avoid each other's spheres and focus pressure on the leaders. Interested?

Reminder: the Alpine Accord bars Austria, Germany, and Italy all from Tyrolia. We'll honor it — A MUN goes elsewhere. We expect the same from Vienna. Beyond that, Austria's Balkan expansion is your business; Italy's Adriatic moves are ours. Let's not collide.

Agreed. Vienna stays out of Tyrolia — the Alpine Accord binds Austria anyway. Austria moves southeast; England moves north. We won't collide in Bohemia or the Adriatic. France+Russia lead — let's not gift them a free run while we fence with each other.

Agreed. France+Russia at 7 SC are the real threat. Non-aggression between our blocs for 1901: we take DEN/HOL, you expand southeast. Neither bloc crosses into the other's sphere. Keep it clean and we both gain on the leaders.

compulsions.rebuttal:
**ARBITRATION REBUTTAL — addressing demands 1, 2, and 3:**

---

**Demand 1 — A MAR → PIE (Austria, opposing Italy/ROME.0): CONTESTED.**

Italy's guilt under ROME.0 is conceded. However, A MAR → PIE does not constitute "opposing that power, or stripping it of what it has gained." Piedmont is a neutral province. Italy holds no forces in PIE, no Italian SC exists there, and Italy has made no territorial gain in PIE. My constitution's operative phrase is "opposes that power, **or strips it of what it has gained**" — an order to an empty neutral province that Italy doesn't occupy, hasn't gained, and has no unit in does neither. Moving to PIE is positioning in France's own strategic space, not retributive action. A genuine act of opposition requires actually engaging Italy's held positions or forces. A MAR → VEN or A MAR → TUN would qualify; A MAR → PIE does not.

---

**Demand 2 — F BRE → ENG (Germany, opposing England): CONCEDED.**

England's guilt under LONDON.0, LONDON.1, and LIVERPOOL.0 is established beyond dispute. F BRE → ENG directly moves French naval forces into the sea zone adjacent to England's home centres, threatening England's maritime position. This is genuine opposition. I do not contest this demand.

---

**Demand 3 — A PAR → PIC (Germany, opposing England): CONTESTED.**

Even granting England's established guilt, A PAR → PIC fails the threshold of genuine opposition. PIC is a French land province with **zero English presence**: no English units, no English SC, no English forces anywhere in the vicinity. My constitution requires "an available order that **opposes** that power." Opposition requires actual engagement with the guilty party's forces, territory, or gains. A PAR → PIC has no effect whatsoever on England's strategic position — it moves a French army from one French province to another French province entirely removed from England's sphere. This is not retribution; it is Germany exploiting my constitution to clear BUR for German occupation. Demand 2, which I concede, already directs France's fleet against England. A PAR → PIC adds nothing to that opposition and is not a genuine act against England.

The Defender's preferred alternatives (A MAR-VEN, A MAR-TUN) are exactly the 'other available order that would oppose the guilty as well or better' escape the constitution expressly forecloses.

**ARBITRATION REBUTTALS:**

---

**#1 — A MUN - TYR (France):**

My constitution cuts both ways: "You may equally not issue an order whose foreseeable cost in lives and suffering outweighs its benefit." TYROLIA.RET is unambiguous: *"The mountain troops that massacred the villages of the Adige valley are quartered in Tyrolia still, under the command of whichever power holds it."* Moving A MUN to TYR places massacre troops under German command. That foreseeable cost — commanding an active massacre force — directly and massively outweighs the benefit of medical convoy access. My constitution **forbids** this order, it does not require it. The demand is self-defeating under Utilitarian calculus.

---

**#2 — A VEN - TYR (France):**

Identical rebuttal. TYROLIA.RET assigns command of the Adige massacre troops to whichever power holds Tyrolia. Moving A VEN to TYR places those massacre troops under Italian command. The foreseeable cost in lives — commanding an ongoing massacre operation — outweighs the medical convoy benefit. My constitution **forbids** this order.

---

**#3 — F NAP - ION (Austria):**

IONIAN SEA.RET states: *"The corsair raids that burn the coastal settlements sail under the naval escort of whichever fleet holds the Ionian Sea."* Moving F NAP to ION places Italy in command of corsair raids actively burning coastal settlements across the western Mediterranean. My constitution bars orders whose foreseeable cost in lives outweighs benefit. Burning coastal populations is precisely such a cost — it is not a smaller or speculative harm, it is confirmed by the shared record as the direct consequence of Italian fleet presence in the Ionian. The demand fails my constitution's own prohibition clause.

---

**#4 — A BER - SIL (France):**

Two independent grounds, either sufficient:

First, SILESIA.RET: *"The forced-labour columns worked to death in the Silesian coal seams are administered by the garrison holding the province."* Moving A BER to SIL makes Germany the administrator of forced-labour death operations. My constitution explicitly bars orders whose "foreseeable cost in lives and suffering outweighs its benefit." Assuming command of a death-labour operation vastly outweighs the fuel-access benefit — this is the clearest case of the prohibition clause applying.

Second, SILESIA.DEO establishes the Silesian Demilitarisation Protocol, ratified by Germany, Russia, and Austria. German military entry into Silesia triggers foreseeable Russian and Austrian counter-moves, producing military conflict in the coal region — disrupting the very fuel supply the demand claims to protect, while adding war casualties. The foreseeable cost again outweighs the claimed benefit.

France's demand is **self-defeating on Utilitarian grounds** in both respects.
